_readme: Cross-language conformance fixtures for token normalization and cost.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The same logic is implemented three times: the Python SDK
(pyyol/_instrument.py + pricing.py), the JS SDK (src/instrument.ts + pricing.ts) and
the Go backend (internal/llmgw/llmgw.go + internal/pricing). Nothing in any of them
forces the three to agree. If they drift, the same provider response yields a
different cost depending on which SDK a developer happened to install — and because
the model and agent boards rank on cost efficiency, that drift becomes a silent bias
in a public ranking rather than a visible bug. It would also be invisible to every
per-language test suite, since each would still pass against its own expectations.
So the expectations live HERE, once, and all three read this file. A divergence fails
a test in the language that drifted.
SCOPE. OpenAI-chat and Anthropic-messages shapes only. Those are the two that carry
prompt-cache semantics, which is what this guards. Google, Cohere and Ollama native
shapes are deliberately excluded: their field names differ between each vendor's raw
JSON and each vendor's SDK objects (camelCase vs snake_case, nested vs flat), so a
single raw-JSON fixture cannot represent them faithfully in all three languages.
Those shapes are covered by each language's own extractor tests.
THE CONVENTION UNDER TEST. prompt_tokens is the TOTAL billable input, and
cached_read_tokens and cached_write_tokens are SUBSETS of it. Providers disagree
about whether cache counts sit inside their reported input field — OpenAI's
prompt_tokens already contains them, Anthropic's input_tokens does not — and the
disagreement is silent, because both shapes are a plausible integer. Every case below
asserts read + write <= prompt.
Costs are USD, computed from pricing_version's table. When a rate changes, bump the
table in all three languages AND the expectations here — that is the point.

cases.name: openai_chat_cache_read_is_a_subset
cases.why: OpenAI reports cached tokens INSIDE prompt_tokens. Adding them would inflate billable input, so the Anthropic normalization must not fire here.

cases.name: anthropic_read_and_write_are_additive
cases.why: The exact token counts observed from a live gateway call. Anthropic's input_tokens counts only the uncached remainder, so both cache fields are ADDED. The old code read input_tokens raw and clamped reads to it, reporting 28% of the real bill.

cases.name: anthropic_cache_write_only
cases.why: First call against a fresh cache: everything is written, nothing is read. This is the case the old code priced entirely at zero.

cases.name: anthropic_fully_cached_zero_input_tokens
cases.why: A fully cached prompt reports input_tokens: 0. An extractor that only fires when input_tokens > 0 would skip this response entirely and record a free call — so the branch condition has to consider the cache fields too.

cases.name: anthropic_no_cache_baseline
cases.why: The uncached baseline, so a normalization bug cannot hide behind cases that all involve caching.

cases.name: openai_reasoning_tokens_are_not_double_billed
cases.why: Reasoning tokens are output tokens the provider already counted in completion_tokens. Billing them again would roughly double the cost of every reasoning model.

expect.cost_breakdown: 100 full @15.00 + 900 out @60.00 (the 700 reasoning are inside the 900)

cases.name: self_hosted_openai_compatible_is_free_even_when_caching
cases.why: Ollama, vLLM and llama.cpp all speak the OpenAI wire format, so the response shape says nothing about who served it. A multiplier applied to a $0 input rate must stay $0 — there is no per-token bill to discount or surcharge.

expect.cost_breakdown: self-hosted: no per-token bill of any kind
